svg.title: Four Weeks to Act on Mineral Market Moves
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-market-response-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Four Weeks to Act on Mineral Market Moves; subtitle: Deductions, pricing, operator capital and new-gas offers; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Audit deductions on every statement; deliverable: Post-production deductions (20% to 35%) compared against the lease's gross-proceeds language; gate: Flywheel deducted under a net-proceeds statute despite gross proceeds leases until a court ruling stopped it; week: Week 2; title: Reprice royalties off the futures strip; deliverable: Strip minus basis, set against buyers anchoring on $50 to $70 oil; gate: No household budget on spot spikes; checks reflect a monthly weighted average and arrive about two months late; week: Week 3; title: Read the operator's investor presentation; deliverable: Where cash flow and rigs are actually going, beyond the headlines; gate: Expect buybacks and dividends first and a one to two quarter lag before rigs respond; week: Week 4; title: Screen helium, pipeline and re-promoter offers; deliverable: Scout cards scanned for non-flammable gas, measured against Rynott's 0.5% to 1.5% helium, 3 to 6 MMcf/d and 10 to 20 location screen; gate: No helium lease to a re-promoter, and no blind pipeline final offer; a $21,000 offer became about a $7M verdict while typical protesters win 10% to 20% more; caption: Price spikes reach royalty checks about two months late, and rigs respond one to two quarters later, so act on statements and operator plans rather than headlines.; assumptions note: The weekly sequence is an organizing frame for the testified checks. The Matterhorn award is under appeal, and the long-term oil view ranges from Sands' $60 to $70 to Josh Young's roughly $105.; note: Attributed to Matt Sands with Justin Williams (n2MrqKJ_h80, M3eFdVkW_mY, oHhvtjxLX9c, FDXztudBSFk, ptrz57qzl54), guest Tim Rynott and Bison Interests' Josh Young on YouTube.
